top_authentic_signals.name: Thermal Noise & Sensor Consistency
top_authentic_signals.summary: The image shows consistent, subtle grain in nearly all regions (0.0% smooth blocks, variance 1372.7) - the expected fingerprint of a real camera sensor.
top_authentic_signals.what_found: Only 0.0% of pixel blocks are flat - the rest carry a consistent, fine-grained texture at the sub-pixel level. This is the natural noise floor left by photon shot noise and thermal read noise on real camera sensors. The variance of 1372.7 is healthy: present but controlled, suggesting base-ISO capture with standard noise reduction.
top_authentic_signals.why_it_matters: Uniform, subtle grain that's present everywhere but never overwhelming is genuinely difficult for AI to replicate convincingly. This pattern - real grain without being suspiciously chaotic - is one of the stronger authentic fingerprints this test can find.
top_authentic_signals.caveat: Heavy compression, denoising, upscaling, or added grain filters can all change the noise profile independently of whether the image was generated or photographed.

top_ai_signals.name: Metadata & Provenance
top_ai_signals.summary: The file's embedded provenance marks it as AI-generated.
top_ai_signals.what_found: The provenance metadata flags this as trained-algorithmic (AI-generated) media.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: Provenance markers like C2PA are an industry-standard, hard-to-fake trace written by the generator itself. Finding one is among the strongest provenance signals available.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Provenance can be stripped or, rarely, forged. Absence of a marker is not proof of authenticity.

top_ai_signals.name: Spectral Artifacts
top_ai_signals.summary: The Six-Lens model scored this image 90.5% AI / 9.5% authentic — a extremely high-confidence finding toward synthetic generation.
top_ai_signals.what_found: All six spectral lenses — visual texture (ConvNeXt), frequency grids (FFT), sensor noise simulation (SRM), color-space fingerprints (YCbCr), spatial reconstruction (SPAI), and robustness testing — collectively scored this image 90.5% AI. A score this strong, the majority of lenses independently flagged patterns like periodic frequency grids and noise distributions inconsistent with any known camera sensor profile.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This model looks for patterns invisible to the human eye — buried in the pixel-level math of the image. A 90.5% score means the statistical fingerprint aligns significantly more with AI generation than camera physics, and these frequency-domain traces are very hard to remove without visibly degrading the image.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Heavy JPEG compression, aggressive resizing, or strong image filters can partially destroy the frequency-domain signals this model depends on, potentially softening a confident AI detection into an inconclusive result. Conversely, very new or unusual AI generators not present in training data may produce lower-than-expected scores.

top_ai_signals.name: Lighting Physics & Contrast Geometry
top_ai_signals.summary: The lighting looks physically impossible for a real camera: dynamic range of 255/255 with only 0.004% blown highlights and 0.002% crushed shadows.
top_ai_signals.what_found: This image spans 255/255 of tonal range but loses virtually no detail at either extreme - 0.004% clipped highlights and 0.002% crushed shadows. Real camera sensors physically cannot do this: they must sacrifice highlight or shadow detail in high-contrast scenes. The regional contrast variance of 593.1 is also suspiciously low, meaning light is distributed unnaturally evenly across the entire scene.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This 'perfect HDR' profile is a known fingerprint of AI generation. Diffusion models compute light mathematically and don't face the physical saturation limits that real sensors do. A camera would always clip in one or both directions here.
top_ai_signals.caveat: HDR post-processing, tone mapping, strong flash, and professional retouching can all alter exposure profiles - introducing 'AI-like' qualities into real photos or vice versa.

top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: Re-saving at quality 90 produced a mean residual of 1.30 with a quadrant spread of only 0.32. The compression stress is consistent across all four quadrants, and only 0.00% of pixels show elevated residuals. This uniform profile suggests the image has a consistent compression history - no obvious signs of region-level editing or compositing.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: A uniform ELA profile removes one red flag - there are no obvious editing seams. However, ELA does not tell us whether the image is AI-generated, only that it has not been obviously composited. The other detectors handle the AI vs. real question.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: ELA detects editing and compression inconsistency, not AI generation. Social media uploads, repeated saves, and WhatsApp forwarding all degrade this test. It's treated as a weak supporting check.
